message.content:
Lions (Panthera leo) and zebras (Equus quagga) belong to very different mammalian orders—Carnivora and Perissodactyla, respectively.  
Their most recent common ancestor is therefore the last common ancestor of the clade that contains both of those orders, i.e. the last common ancestor of all placental mammals (Eutheria).  

That ancestor lived roughly 100–110 million years ago, during the early Cretaceous, before the major diversification of modern mammalian orders.
